Subject: Security bundle + quick checklist for Nova Health review

Hi Ellie / Connor,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the candid overview of what Nova Health is trying to solve. As promised, attaching the SOC 2 packet and a short checklist we use for first-pass compliance reviews. Key items from our side: 

- What we shared: Redwood_SOC2_Packet_20260820.pdf (SOC 2 Type II summary + controls matrix), network_diagram.png (high-level network topology).
- Typical review asks we see from health-tech customers: data residency options, encryption/keys, logging/audit retention, and onboarding timeline.
- Suggested next step: quick 30-minute sync between your security lead and our technical compliance engineer to walk through any blockers.

If it helps, here’s a one-line recap of the timeline we discussed on the call: Nova aims to finalize vendor compliance checks in the next 2–3 weeks; if anything changes on your side please flag it and we can adjust.

Can you confirm who from your team will be best to take the SOC 2 packet? I can coordinate a short walkthrough (30 min) next week.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez

Hi Diego —

Thanks for the follow-up and apologies for the delayed response; we had a couple of internal meetings this week. We received the packet and Connor (cc’d) will be leading the review. Two quick notes from our initial pass:

1) Data residency: can Redwood guarantee EU-only storage for PHI-derived embeddings, or do you offer a configuration to route data through EU-only regions?
2) Key management: we need to understand if Redwood supports a BYOK model (customer-managed keys) or integrates with our KMS — specifically KMS provider options and whether keys can be restricted by region.

We also attached a short internal checklist (Nova_Quick_Compliance_Notes.docx) with a few fields we’ll need filled to move forward. Can we get answers to the two items above and a rough timeline? We expect to complete vendor checks in ~2 weeks but would like to request a brief extension if deeper technical details are required.

Happy to set a 30-minute meeting next week including Connor if that helps — Connor, can you suggest availability?

Thanks,
Ellie Summers
Head of Partnerships, Nova Health
ellie@novahealth.ai | +1 (617) 555-0123

Attachment: Nova_Quick_Compliance_Notes.docx (docx, 45KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellie Summers <ellie@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Connor Blake <connor.blake@novahealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security bundle + quick checklist for Nova Health review

Hi Ellie / Connor —

Great, thanks for the pointer — totally understand the need for a bit more time. Short answers up-front:

- Data residency: yes — we can pin storage and inference to specific regions. For PHI-derived artifacts we support EU region pinning and can provide documentation on how we segregate those datasets.
- Key management: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via integrations with major KMS providers and also offer Redwood-hosted KMS with region scoping. I’ll have Priyom (cc’d) share the exact KMS vendors and a short note on the technical steps to enable BYOK for a private deployment.

If you’d like, let’s schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week to go over the checklist and any technical details. Proposed times (PT):
- Tue 8 Sep, 10:00–10:30
- Wed 9 Sep, 14:00–14:30
- Thu 10 Sep, 09:00–09:30

Priyom will join to answer technical questions and walk through the KMS/KV cache behavior for regional pinning. If a different time zone works better for you, I can adjust.

Thanks — happy to extend the review window on our side; let me know which slot works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Diego is one of the Redwood Inference sales team; Priyom Das is listed as the technical compliance contact.
